caption:
Two lineages build your brain, and they never mix.
Nature Neuroscience, 18 Sept 2026. Dundes, Jokhai, Loh and colleagues, Stanford Medicine.

Two cell lineages, Otx2 and Gbx2, build the brain from gastrulation onward and never mix, traced in mouse embryos. The same split appears in chick, zebrafish and acorn worms, lineages that diverged around 550 million years ago. Loh lab, Stanford Medicine. Nature Neuroscience, 18 Sept 2026. 'Two organs' is press framing; the paper shows two lineages.

#neuroscience #brain #evolution #science
voiceover_script: Your brain is built by two cell lineages that never mix. In the mouse embryo, two separate populations of stem cells build the brain, and they are separate from gastrulation onward. One group, marked by a gene called Otx2, builds the forebrain and midbrain. The other, marked by Gbx2, builds the hindbrain. They carry different chromatin states from the earliest stages. The same split shows up in chicks, zebrafish and acorn worms, lineages that diverged around five hundred and fifty million years ago. One caveat. The paper describes two cell lineages, traced in mice. Two organs is the press release talking.
